author.name: William Shakespeare
author.biography: Shakespeare left Stratford-upon-Avon for a career in London's theatres, where he worked as an actor, playwright and company shareholder. He knew stories as things people performed before other people, with attention, sympathy and judgment changing from moment to moment. Shakespeare made kings answerable to the same needs as their subjects: shelter, affection and honest speech. Lear's royal household lets those needs collide with the habits of command.

hook.text: Would you rather be loved or told how much you are loved?

paragraphs: Lear wants to divide his kingdom and keep the privileges of being king. Before deciding who receives what, he asks his daughters to declare their love.

The request makes affection into a public competition. Beautiful language can win material rewards; an awkward truth can look like disobedience. The difficulty is larger than one family's quarrel. What happens when authority loses the ability to distinguish devotion from performance?

As familiar protections weaken, the play turns towards what people require simply to remain human. Clothing, company and a place to sleep acquire a force they seldom possess inside a palace. Shakespeare also makes care appear in people and gestures that official measures of loyalty fail to recognise.
Read for who can speak honestly without being heard, and who learns to listen after the cost has become terrible. If your position stopped protecting you, how would you know whose love could survive?

orientation.text: Lear's family story develops alongside Gloucester's. Keep the two households distinct; their similarities are part of the play's design.
